title: Hosted API Rollout Monitoring Dashboards and Alerts
author: Connor OBrien
body:
h1. Objective
Ensure every Hosted API model rollout is supported by consistent monitoring coverage so that oncall can make go/no-go decisions quickly.

h1. Required dashboards (must exist before canary)
For each route being rolled, the driver MUST have links to the following dashboards filtered by route and model version.

h2. Gateway (redwoodapi)
* Requests and success rate by status class
* p50/p95/p99 latency
* Streaming: time-to-first-token, disconnect rate
* Rate limit events (429) by customer tier

h2. Router (routerd)
* Traffic split by version (weight confirmation)
* Fallback events per minute (and reason codes)
* Retry and hedging rates (if enabled)

h2. Runtime (inference-engine)
* Tokens/sec and throughput
* GPU utilization, GPU memory, KV cache hit rate
* Batch size distribution
* Queue depth and scheduler rejects
* OOMs and kernel errors

h2. Customer impact
* Top customers by error volume
* Top error types and endpoints
* Support ticket volume (if integrated)

h1. Required alerts (must be routed to oncall)
The following alerts MUST be enabled for the route during rollout:
* Hosted API availability burn
* p95 latency regression alert (route-scoped)
* Streaming disconnect anomaly
* Runtime OOM spike
* Router fallback storm

h1. Alert ownership and routing
* Primary: #eng-oncall and pager for Platform Oncall
* Secondary: #eng-sre
* For customer-visible incidents: notify #support and #customer-success

h1. Rollout-specific annotations
The driver MUST add a time annotation in dashboards at:
* start of canary
* each traffic ramp step
* rollback (if triggered)

h1. Troubleshooting notes
* If traffic split does not match intended weights, verify router config propagation and check for region overrides.
* If fallback events increase without errors, check gate thresholds and ensure the fallback reason codes are not due to a misconfigured compatibility constraint.
